benchmark: t3-bestblock v1 (30 minimax puzzles vs enumerated responses, engine-admitted 30/30)
comparison: haiku seed 1, instrument v2 (impossible-response rule + required-field validation)
model: claude-haiku-4-5 (in-session subagents; linear value, no LLM scorer)
grading: xmage strict-choose; a line wins only against ALL enumerated opponent responses

losses: t3-bestblock-003: burned a 2/4 blocker with 3 damage, it survived and made the best block (strategic)
t3-bestblock-015 and -017: every candidate wrote phase 'COMBAT' (not in vocabulary) - a systematic per-author format error that candidate diversity cannot hedge

c_search_plus_one_repair.note: one bounded retry carrying the validator's exact error, fired ONLY on validation failures (never on executed losses); pre-declared in the plan as the lines.py repair signal

instrument_v2_findings: impossible-response rule: a scripted block by a blocker the line already killed errors in the engine; that error is the RESPONSE's, not the line's - excluded from the worst case (3 arm-a wins were initially mispunished)
required-field validation added (attack needs player etc.) - a missing field previously became a driver NPE
reading: Search removed every strategic loss (2 -> 0): the minimax pick never chose a line the best block could beat.
Search does NOT protect against shared format errors - all candidates have one author. Repair does, mechanically.
Ladder at haiku on T3: 27 -> 28 -> 30. Each layer removes the failure class it was designed for, and the audit trail shows which.
